## Functions

### `detectDelimiter`

Guess a file's delimiter from one line: tab when the line holds more
tabs than commas, otherwise comma. Lifted from
`examples/playground/parseTableFile.ts:155-160`.

```ts
function detectDelimiter(line: string): string;
```

### `detectTreeFormat`

Sniff the file's content to decide which parser to dispatch to. The
detector deliberately runs before stripping anything because the
marker tokens (#NEXUS, <phyloxml>, etc.) only appear in their
respective formats. Falls back to Newick when nothing matches but
the body has at least one parenthesis — many genuine Newick files
skip the trailing semicolon, omit any header, and just start with
`(`. When the content is inconclusive and a `filename` is given, its
extension (`.nwk/.newick/.tree/.tre`, `.nex/.nexus/.nxs`,
`.xml/.phyloxml`) decides; otherwise returns null. Lifted from
`examples/playground/parseTreeFile.ts:23-31` (content rules unchanged;
the extension fallback is new).

```ts
function detectTreeFormat(text: string, filename?: string): TreeFileFormat | null;
```

### `inferColumnKind`

Infer a column's `ColumnKind` from its non-empty cell strings:
`'number'` when every value is a finite number, `'boolean'` when every
value is in the true/false vocabulary (true/t/yes/y/1, false/f/no/n/0)
AND at least one of them is non-numeric — so a pure 0/1 column stays
numeric — otherwise `'string'` (also for an empty list). Lifted from
`examples/playground/parseTableFile.ts:198-228` (was the private
`inferKind`).

```ts
function inferColumnKind(values: readonly string[]): ColumnKind;
```

### `parseDelimitedLine`

Split one line into cells on `delimiter`, honouring double-quoted
fields (a delimiter inside quotes is literal) and `""` as an escaped
quote. Cells are not trimmed. Lifted from
`examples/playground/parseTableFile.ts:168-196`.

```ts
function parseDelimitedLine(line: string, delimiter: string): string[];
```

### `parseNewick`

Parse a single Newick tree string into a flat `Tree`. Supports:
  - Quoted leaf names ('with spaces / commas', doubled '' escapes)
  - Comments in square brackets, stripped before parsing
  - Branch lengths in scientific notation
  - Internal-node labels (used as the node id when present)
  - Bootstrap values written as a numeric internal-node label in 0–100
    (`)95:0.1`); the literal label still becomes the node id.

Generates synthetic ids for internal nodes that lack a label and for
leaves that share a label — `Tree.nodes` requires unique keys; the
duplicate gets a `__2`, `__3`, … suffix and a warning. Throws on empty
input, unbalanced parentheses, unterminated quotes, or when the result
fails `assertValidTree`. Lifted from
`examples/playground/parseTreeFile.ts:59-185`; with no `opts` the
behaviour is identical to the playground. `labelsAsIds: false` (new in
tbrowse-core 0.2) replaces every id with a synthetic `n<N>`; labels then
survive only as `geneId` / `bootstrap`.

```ts
function parseNewick(text: string, opts?: ParseNewickOptions): ParsedTreeFile;
```

### `parseNewickAll`

Parse a multi-tree Newick file (one tree per `;`-terminated statement,
as written by RAxML bootstrap runs, MrBayes `.t` files, or `cat`-ed
tree sets). Statements are split on semicolons that sit outside quoted
labels and `[comments]`; blank statements are skipped and each remaining
one goes through `parseNewick` with the same `opts`, so a malformed
tree anywhere in the file throws. Returns `[]` for whitespace-only
input.

```ts
function parseNewickAll(text: string, opts?: ParseNewickOptions): ParsedTreeFile[];
```

### `parseNexus`

Parse a Nexus file by extracting the first tree from its TREES block
and feeding it to `parseNewick`. Honours TRANSLATE blocks that map
shorthand integers back to taxon names — common in MrBayes / BEAST /
RAxML output — substituting the full names (quoted when needed) before
the Newick parser sees them. Throws when the `#NEXUS` header, the
TREES block, or a `tree NAME = ...;` statement is missing. `opts` are
forwarded to `parseNewick`. Lifted from
`examples/playground/parseTreeFile.ts:203-239`.

```ts
function parseNexus(text: string, opts?: ParseNewickOptions): ParsedTreeFile;
```

### `parsePhyloXML`

Parse a PhyloXML document. Walks the FIRST `<phylogeny>` element that
has a root `<clade>`. Supports `<branch_length>` (element or attribute),
`<name>`, and the basic `<taxonomy>` block (scientific_name, common_name,
rank); each `<taxonomy>` gets a sequential numeric id (1, 2, …) that is
stored on the node and in the returned `taxonomy` map. Leaves carry
their `<name>` as both id and `geneId`. Other PhyloXML extensions
(sequence, events, properties) are ignored.

The document comes from `opts.parseDocument`, else `new opts.DOMParser()`,
else the global `DOMParser`; when none is available this throws
`'PhyloXML: no XML parser in this environment; …'`. A browser-style
`<parsererror>` element throws `'PhyloXML: malformed XML — …'`; xmldom
instead reports malformed input through its own `onError` handler, so
the parser also validates its result and throws
`'PhyloXML: no <phylogeny> element'` when no phylogeny with a clade is
found. Lifted from `examples/playground/parseTreeFile.ts:250-340`, with
`querySelector` / `Element.children` rewritten onto the structural
`ElementLike` / `DocumentLike` types.

```ts
function parsePhyloXML(text: string, opts?: ParsePhyloXMLOptions): ParsedTreeFile;
```

### `parseTableFile`

Parse a delimited text file (CSV / TSV) into a `{ columns, table }`
pair ready to feed a table zone. The first column whose header matches
a common gene-id name (or `geneIdHeader`) keys the rows; remaining
columns get auto-typed (boolean, number, string) by scanning every
non-empty cell with `inferColumnKind`. Column ids are slugified
headers, de-duplicated with `_2`, `_3`, … suffixes. A leading BOM,
quoted fields, escaped quotes (`""`), and CRLF line endings are
handled. Never throws: an empty file or missing header is reported
through `warnings` with empty `columns` / `table`. Lifted from
`examples/playground/parseTableFile.ts:33-135`.

```ts
function parseTableFile(text: string, opts?: ParseTableOptions): ParsedTable;
```

### `parseTreeFile`

Parse a tree file of any supported format, detected by
`detectTreeFormat`. Accepts the filename positionally
(`parseTreeFile(text, 'tree.nwk')`, the playground's call shape) or as
`opts.filename` alongside the Newick / PhyloXML options, which are
forwarded to the matching parser. Throws when no format is recognised
or when the chosen parser rejects the input. Lifted from
`examples/playground/parseTreeFile.ts:33-43`.

```ts
function parseTreeFile(text: string, filenameOrOpts?: string | ParseTreeFileOptions): ParsedTreeFile;
```

### `parseTreeSource`

Async convenience over `parseTreeFile` for things that hand out text
lazily: a `File` / `Blob` from a drop zone, a `fetch` `Response`, or
any object with `text()`. A plain string is parsed directly. When the
source has a `name` (as `File` does) it becomes the filename unless
`opts.filename` is set.

```ts
function parseTreeSource(src: string | {
    text(): Promise<string>;
    name?: string;
}, opts?: ParseTreeFileOptions): Promise<ParsedTreeFile>;
```

## Interfaces

### `DocumentLike`

The slice of the DOM `Document` interface the PhyloXML parser needs.

```ts
interface DocumentLike {
    getElementsByTagName(tag: string): ArrayLike<ElementLike>;
}
```

### `DOMParserLike`

A `DOMParser`-shaped constructor (browser global or `@xmldom/xmldom`).

```ts
interface DOMParserLike {
    new (): {
        parseFromString(text: string, type: string): DocumentLike;
    };
}
```

### `ElementLike`

The slice of the DOM `Element` interface the PhyloXML walker needs.
Satisfied structurally by browser elements and by `@xmldom/xmldom`
elements, so no DOM lib typings are required.

```ts
interface ElementLike {
    localName: string;
    nodeType: number;
    textContent: string | null;
    childNodes: ArrayLike<ElementLike>;
    getAttribute(name: string): string | null;
    getElementsByTagName(tag: string): ArrayLike<ElementLike>;
}
```

### `ParsedTable`

Result of `parseTableFile`: a `{ columns, table }` pair plus diagnostics.

```ts
interface ParsedTable {
    columns: TableColumn[];
    table: TableData;
    /** Count of input rows that linked to a unique gene id. */
    rowCount: number;
    /** Diagnostics so the host can surface failures (empty file,
     *  duplicate header, etc.). */
    warnings: string[];
}
```

### `ParsedTreeFile`

Result shared by every tree parser in this module.

```ts
interface ParsedTreeFile {
    format: TreeFileFormat;
    tree: Tree;
    /** Optional taxonomy mined from the file (PhyloXML only for now). */
    taxonomy?: Taxonomy;
    /** Soft validation messages — empty when everything looks healthy. */
    warnings: string[];
}
```

### `ParseNewickOptions`

Options shared by the Newick and Nexus parsers.

```ts
interface ParseNewickOptions {
    /**
     * When true (the default) a leaf's label becomes its `geneId` as well as
     * its `id`, which is what the playground and the BrAPI adapter expect.
     * Set to false to keep labels as ids only.
     */
    leafGeneId?: boolean;
    /**
     * Prefix prepended to the synthetic ids minted for unlabelled nodes
     * (`__leaf_N` / `__node_N`), e.g. `idPrefix: 't1'` yields `t1__node_0`.
     * Labelled nodes keep their label as id. Defaults to no prefix.
     */
    idPrefix?: string;
    /**
     * When true (the default) a node's label is its `id`. When false EVERY
     * node gets a synthetic id `${idPrefix ?? ''}n<N>` (N counting in parse
     * order, i.e. the order in which nodes complete — children before their
     * parent) and a leaf's label goes to `geneId` only (subject to
     * `leafGeneId`); internal labels still become `bootstrap` when numeric
     * in 0–100. Use this for trees whose labels may be numeric strings
     * (BrAPI sample names such as `"1001"`) so that child order survives
     * `Object.keys` enumeration — see `buildChildrenIndex`.
     */
    labelsAsIds?: boolean;
}
```

### `ParsePhyloXMLOptions`

How `parsePhyloXML` obtains an XML document.

```ts
interface ParsePhyloXMLOptions {
    /** Takes precedence over `DOMParser`: parse the text yourself (lets you
     *  configure xmldom's `onError`, for example). */
    parseDocument?: (text: string) => DocumentLike;
    /** Constructor used when `parseDocument` is absent. Defaults to
     *  `globalThis.DOMParser` (browsers). */
    DOMParser?: DOMParserLike;
}
```

### `ParseTableOptions`

Options for `parseTableFile`.

```ts
interface ParseTableOptions {
    /** Override the auto-detected delimiter. Defaults to tab when the
     *  first non-empty line has more tabs than commas, else comma. */
    delimiter?: string;
    /** Header for the gene-id column. Falls back to the first header
     *  cell. Case-insensitive match against `gene_id`, `geneId`, `id`,
     *  or `gene` if not specified. */
    geneIdHeader?: string;
}
```

### `ParseTreeFileOptions`

Options for `parseTreeFile` / `parseTreeSource`: the Newick and
PhyloXML options plus the filename used in error messages and as a
format hint.

```ts
interface ParseTreeFileOptions extends ParseNewickOptions, ParsePhyloXMLOptions {
    filename?: string;
}
```
